rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads the clause as a circumstantial accusative and takes yamh as independent, from yamḥū with an omitted wāw, rather than coordinating it with yakhtim.
rows.anchor: it is an independent sentence. And it is in fact

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi argues that a fabricated Qur’an could not destroy evil and establish truth; a Satanic fabrication would have the opposite effect.
rows.anchor: Fabrication is always from Satan, and Satan is not one who obliterates evil and reinforces the truth

rows.speaker: Jesus
rows.claim: Jesus answers the charge that exorcism works through Beelzebub by asking how Satan’s divided kingdom could endure.
rows.anchor: If Satan casts out Satan, he is divided against himself; how then will his kingdom stand?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusers knowingly spread false claims even though they recognized the Qur’an’s truth and the Prophet’s blameless character, because they refused to accept them.
rows.anchor: those who had worked this mischief fully knew that neither is the

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the accusers’ hidden thoughts and what they say aloud.
rows.anchor: God fully knows the secrets of their hearts; He is aware what is in their hearts and what they say from their tongues

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning invites the accusers to repent while there is still time; God is merciful and pardons His servants.
rows.anchor: opportunity to save themselves from the wrath of God if they do so.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows all they do, and they cannot conceal any of their sins from Him.
rows.anchor: they will not be able to hide any of their sins from Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers who answered the call and did righteous deeds receive added bounty in this world and the next; disbelievers face painful punishment.
rows.anchor: they will be blessed with more favours in this world and the next

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He parses “those who believed” as the subject rather than the object, citing 6:36, where only true hearers accept the message.
rows.anchor: they are in the place of a subject

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The affluent are mistaken if they take their riches as proof that they are on the right path or as grounds for arrogance toward the Prophet and poorer believers.
rows.anchor: if their worldly affluence and riches have led them to believe that they are on the right path

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God apportions wealth to believers and disbelievers according to wisdom and circumstances to test whether they remain patient and grateful; unrestricted riches could lead to rebellion.
rows.anchor: per His wisdom and expedience, and in this manner tries them both.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recipients should thank God rather than credit their own ability or forebears, since He can grant wealth and take it away.
rows.anchor: he should remain grateful to God Who has the authority to give and also to take away after giving.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the subject of wealth distribution is treated in more detail in the following sūrah, al-Zukhruf, which parallels this one.
rows.anchor: This subject is discussed in more detail in the succeeding sūrah: Sūrah al-Zukhruf

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The counterpart sūrah elaborates that God assigns different livelihoods and ranks so people serve one another, while worldly riches are temporary and success belongs to the virtuous.
rows.anchor: We have allocated among them their livelihood in this world and have raised some in status above others

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sends rain when people despair; because livelihood depends on it, this reminds them that neither deities nor human means control their provision.
rows.anchor: sending down rain from the blocked crevices of the sky is only in the hands of the Almighty

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain is an everyday sign that God alone is the true accomplisher and al-Ḥamīd, worthy of good attributes, praise, and gratitude.
rows.anchor: this every day observation shows that the real accomplisher is God and He is

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God continues to sustain people through worldly life even when they challenge Him despite living on His provision.
rows.anchor: people who thrive on his sustenance and even challenge Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation of the heavens and earth demonstrates that God can recreate people; Islahi links this argument to the question in 79:27.
rows.anchor: The God Who has created the heavens and the earth is even more capable of recreating man.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dābbah ordinarily denotes living creatures inhabiting earth; the dual “between them” can include sky creatures because al-samāʾ also means the atmosphere where birds fly.
rows.anchor: it is also used for the atmosphere in which birds fly.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast between scattering and gathering is eloquent proof of resurrection: the One who scattered creatures can gather them, as a farmer gathers a crop from scattered seeds.
rows.anchor: The former means “to scatter” and “to spread,” and the latter “to gather” and “to bring together.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly sorrows result from people’s deeds, though God overlooks many; they warn people that life is not play and that their Creator will gather them to account.
rows.anchor: Whatever sorrows people are afflicted with in this world are because of their own deeds even though God forgoes many of them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s respite does not signal indifference or equal regard for good and evil; He has appointed a coming day of complete recompense.
rows.anchor: He has appointed a day to mete out complete reward and punishment which is bound to come.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word yaʿfū means “to overlook,” a Qur’anic usage found in many places.
rows.anchor: means “to overlook.” It is used in this meaning at many instances in the Qur’ān.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People’s inability to escape calamity or obtain help in this world proves that no deity, intercessor, or supporter will shield them from God’s grasp at Judgment.
rows.anchor: no deity or intercessor nor any helper or supporter will be able to protect them from the grasp of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The addressees are disbelievers, whose worldly calamities arise from their deeds.
rows.anchor: the addressees are the disbelievers, who are inflicted with calamities in this world because of their deeds.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calamities suffered by prophets, the truthful, and the righteous are trials rather than punishment; patience in them raises their status.
rows.anchor: The calamities which they are inflicted with are not because of their deeds but to try and test them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ships serve as a sign of God’s power and wisdom, so people absorbed in worldly success should view life as a sea voyage.
rows.anchor: It is the result of God’s power and wisdom that ships as heavy as the mountains sail in the sea.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People wrongly assume ships are safe while cruising, but God can stop the wind and leave them stranded at sea.
rows.anchor: He can stop the wind and these ships together leaving their passengers are stranded in the sea.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can also sink the ships, with no one able to save their passengers.
rows.anchor: He can even make these ships and their ships drown in the sea with no one to be able to save them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though the parable originally concerns sail-powered ships known in that era, Islahi says it applies equally to modern ships as science teaches people to harness steam.
rows.anchor: this same parable can precisely relate to the modern day ships as well.
